senses.definition: create a vacuum in (a bulb, flask, reaction vessel)
excrete or discharge from the body
move out of an unsafe location into safety
examples: After the earthquake, residents were evacuated

senses.definition: move people from their homes or country
remove content from
the act of evacuating; leaving a place in an orderly fashion; especially for protection
the act of removing the contents of something
the bodily process of discharging waste matter
evaluate or estimate the nature, quality, ability, extent, or significance of
examples: I will have the family jewels appraised by a professional
access all the factors when taking a risk

senses.definition: form a critical opinion of
examples: I cannot judge some works of modern art
How do you evaluate this grant proposal?
We shouldn't pass judgment on other people

senses.definition: act of ascertaining or fixing the value or worth of
an appraisal of the value of something
examples: he set a high valuation on friendship

senses.definition: being level or straight or regular and without variation as e.g. in shape or texture; or being in the same plane or at the same height as something else (i.e. even with)
examples: the road was not very even
the picture is even with the window

senses.definition: divisible by two
equal in degree or extent or amount; or equally matched or balanced
examples: even amounts of butter and sugar
it was a fifty-fifty (or even) split

senses.definition: occurring at fixed intervals
examples: the even rhythm of his breathing

senses.definition: of the score in a contest
symmetrically arranged
in spite of; notwithstanding
examples: even when he is sick, he works
even with his head start she caught up with him

senses.definition: to a greater degree or extent; used with comparisons
examples: looked sick and felt even worse
an even (or still) more interesting problem
still another problem must be solved

senses.definition: to the full extent
used as an intensive especially to indicate something unexpected
examples: declined even to consider the idea
I don't have even a dollar!

senses.definition: the latter part of the day (the period of decreasing daylight from late afternoon until nightfall)
examples: he enjoyed the evening light across the lake

senses.definition: become even or more even
make even or more even
make level or straight
a conventional expression of greeting or farewell, used to wish someone a good evening
a later concluding time period
examples: it was the evening of the Roman Empire

senses.definition: the early part of night (from dinner until bedtime) spent in a special way
the latter part of the day (the period of decreasing daylight from late afternoon until nightfall)
examples: he enjoyed the evening light across the lake

senses.definition: in a level and regular way
in equal amounts or shares; in a balanced or impartial way
examples: a class evenly divided between girls and boys
deal equally with rich and poor

senses.definition: a phenomenon located at a single point in space-time; the fundamental observational entity in relativity theory
a phenomenon that follows and is caused by some previous phenomenon
examples: the magnetic effect was greater when the rod was lengthwise
his decision had depressing consequences for business
he acted very wise after the event

senses.definition: a special set of circumstances
examples: in that event, the first possibility is excluded
it may rain in which case the picnic will be canceled

senses.definition: something that happens at a given place and time
after an unspecified period of time or an especially long delay
(intensifier for adjectives) very
at all times; all the time and on every occasion
examples: I will always be there to help you
there is always some pollution in the air
ever hoping to strike it rich

senses.definition: at any time
examples: the best con man of all time

senses.definition: continuing forever or indefinitely
examples: the ageless themes of love and revenge

senses.definition: without qualification; used informally as (often pejorative) intensifiers
any of various plants of various genera of the family Compositae having flowers that can be dried without loss of form or color
(used of count nouns) each and all of the members of a group considered singly and without exception
each and all of a series of entities or intervals as specified
appropriate for ordinary or routine occasions
commonplace and ordinary
found in the ordinary course of events
examples: there's nothing quite like a real … train conductor to add color to a quotidian commute

senses.definition: all things that are of importance to a person
to or in any or all places; pronoun, location; quantifier: universal
examples: You find fast food stores everywhere
people everywhere are becoming aware of the problem
he carried a gun everywhere he went
looked all over for a suitable gift

senses.definition: (law) all the means by which any alleged matter of fact whose truth is investigated at judicial trial is established or disproved
an indication that makes something evident
examples: his trembling was evidence of his fear

senses.definition: your basis for belief or disbelief; knowledge on which to base belief
examples: the evidence that smoking causes lung cancer is very compelling

senses.definition: give evidence
examples: he was telling on all his former colleague

senses.definition: provide evidence for
examples: The blood test showed that he was the father
Her behavior testified to her incompetence

senses.definition: provide evidence for; stand as proof of; show by one's behavior, attitude, or external attributes
examples: His high fever attested to his illness
The buildings in Rome manifest a high level of architectural sophistication
This decision demonstrates his sense of fairness

senses.definition: capable of being seen or noticed
examples: a clearly evident erasure in the manuscript

senses.definition: clearly revealed to the mind or the senses or judgment
examples: the effects of the drought are apparent to anyone who sees the parched fields
it is plain that he is no reactionary

senses.definition: unmistakably (‘plain’ is often used informally for ‘plainly’)
examples: she was in bed and evidently in great pain
he was manifestly too important to leave off the guest list
she has apparently been living here for some time
I thought he owned the property, but apparently not

senses.definition: having or exerting a malignant influence
having the nature of vice
morally bad or wrong
morally objectionable behavior
the quality of being morally wrong in principle or practice
examples: attempts to explain the origin of evil in the world

senses.definition: call forth (emotions, feelings, and responses)
call to mind
examples: These pictures bring back sad memories

senses.definition: deduce (a principle) or construe (a meaning)
examples: We drew out some interesting linguistic data from the native informant

senses.definition: evoke or provoke to appear or occur
examples: Her behavior provoked a quarrel between the couple

senses.definition: summon into action or bring into existence, often as if by magic
examples: he conjured wild birds in the air
call down the spirits from the mountain

senses.definition: (biology) the sequence of events involved in the evolutionary development of a species or taxonomic group of organisms
a process in which something passes by degrees to a different stage (especially a more advanced or mature stage)
examples: the development of his ideas took many years
the slow development of her skill as a writer

senses.definition: gain through experience
examples: I acquired a strong aversion to television
Children must develop a sense of right and wrong
Dave developed leadership qualities in his new position

senses.definition: undergo development or evolution
examples: Modern man evolved a long time ago

senses.definition: work out
examples: We have developed a new theory of evolution
